title: I'm making a racing game where you don't drive: you train an AI to drive for you. Is this concept fun or am I crazy?
author: Lightnig125
selftext:
Hey everyone!



I've been working on a mobile racing game with a twist: you never drive. Instead, you raise a little AI driver that learns by itself through evolution (a real neural network, trained live on your phone, not generative AI).



At generation 0 it's a disaster: cars spin, crash, and blame the wall. You watch it improve generation after generation (speed it up to x16 if you're impatient), until it actually takes corners and drifts.



What you control:

\- The training team: each car has a personality. The Pilot, Granny (careful, hates walls), the Mad Scientist (random mutations, genius or crash), the Copycat, the Speeder.

\- A research tree: unlock new "senses" for your AI (see corners further away, feel how tight a turn is, a bigger brain...). It then has to learn to use them.

\- A garage: swap cars and parts. Each choice is a trade-off (faster but less grip...), and your AI has to adapt to its new ride.

\- Races: put your AI against copies of itself or your other AIs.



Coming next: multiplayer. Your AI will race the AIs trained by other players, with a ranked ladder and competitions. Whose AI is the best driver in the world? You won't be behind the wheel, but it's still your driver, trained your way.



It's still early, and I'd really love your honest opinion on the concept itself:

1. Would you enjoy a racing game where you coach instead of drive?

2. Is watching your AI learn satisfying enough, or would you get bored?

3. Which part sounds the most fun: training, research, garage, or racing?

4. What would make you come back to it every day?



Brutal feedback welcome, that's exactly what I need. Thanks!

comments.author: Infinitecontextlabs
comments.body:
Love the concept and would love to try it out 

1. Yes probably.
2. Watching will be satisfying to begin with but may get boring over time.
3. Research and training.
4. I'm not sure yet. Maybe nothing?
